subject.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap

question: Should OpenShell enforce an unconditional 100 MiB maximum for every sandbox bridge read, including existing workloads that may legitimately read larger files?
rationale: The cap is a deliberate sandbox resource boundary that prevents unbounded host allocation but changes runtime behavior for all larger reads; code review cannot establish the product-compatible threshold alone.

options.title: Confirm the 100 MiB contract
options.body: Approve the fixed ceiling after the contributor provides current-head runtime proof for both normal and oversized reads.

options.title: Choose a different boundary
options.body: Specify a different cap or a documented owner-controlled policy if known OpenShell workloads require reads above 100 MiB.

recommendation.title: Confirm the 100 MiB contract
recommendation.body: Approve the fixed ceiling after the contributor provides current-head runtime proof for both normal and oversized reads.

likelyOwner.reason: An owner familiar with supported OpenShell sandbox workloads is needed to confirm the new resource boundary.
